parameters.note: Saxon Creek is not named in CCR §7.40(b) or §7.50(b), so it follows the general statewide stream regulation §5.85(a)(2): open all year, with a 5-trout harvest season from the last Saturday in April through Nov. 15 and a 0-trout, artificial-lures-with-barbless-hooks catch-and-release season from Nov. 16 through the Friday before the last Saturday in April. Although Saxon Creek lies in the Lake Tahoe basin, it is NOT a direct 'Tahoe Lake tributary'. It is a tributary of Trout Creek, joining it in Lake Valley (Wikipedia: 'It is joined by Saxon Creek in Lake Valley'); Trout Creek in turn flows north through Lake Christopher and the Truckee Marsh into the south shore of Lake Tahoe. The Lake Tahoe tributary special closure §7.50(b)(152)(A) reaches only 'Tahoe Lake tributaries upstream to the first lake' — and the first lake/impoundment on the Trout Creek stem is Lake Christopher (a dammed lake at the Cold Creek confluence, ~38.914,-119.965), which lies downstream (north) of where Saxon Creek joins Trout Creek (~38.883,-119.980); Saxon Creek therefore sits ABOVE the first lake and outside the §7.50(b)(152)(A) special reach. It is also outside §7.50(b)(161) ('Upper Truckee River and tributaries upstream from confluence with Showers Creek'), which governs a different drainage (the Upper Truckee River, not Trout Creek). This mirrors the treatment of Angora Creek, another Lake Tahoe-basin sub-tributary that falls under §5.85(a)(2). A stricter reading — treating any water in the Lake Tahoe drainage as a §7.50(b)(152)(A) Tahoe tributary — is possible; verify against the current CDFW booklet. candidates.summary: Open all year under the general statewide stream regulation: harvest season (last Saturday in April through Nov. 15, 5 trout) and a zero-trout catch-and-release season (Nov. 16 through the Friday before the last Saturday in April, artificial lures with barbless hooks only). Not subject to a Lake Tahoe tributary special closure (it is a sub-tributary of Trout Creek, above the first lake).
